question.leadin: This man was the first president of Gran Colombia, and he won the battles of Boyaca and Carabobo.
question.text: Name this South American leader known as "The Liberator."
question.answerHtml: Simón Bolívar [or Simón José Antonio de la Santísima Trinidad Bolívar Palacios Ponte y Blanco]
question.clue: This man attacked Francisco de Miranda's failed republic in the Cartagena Manifesto.

swap.text: The Contras were from this Central American country.
swap.clue: In the 1990's, this country's rule passed from the FSLN to the opposition led by Violeta de Chamorro.

question.text: In the 17th and 18th centuries, galleon trade flourished between Manila and this Mexican city, whose bay forms a notable beach resort today.
question.clue: This Mexican port city. Under the rule of New Spain, it was granted a monopoly on the Manila galleon trade.

swap.text: This next largest Caribbean island, the most populous island in the Americas, contains the nations of Haiti and the Dominican Republic.
swap.clue: An independence movement on this island called La Trinitaria was led by Juan Pablo Duarte.

question.leadin: Soldiers from this country were sent overseas to fight in a civil war during Operation Carlota.
question.text: Name this country whose Communist government sent troops to aid the MPLA in Angola. This country's communist government came to power after a revolution overthrowing military dictator Fulgencio Batista.
question.clue: The independence hero Guillermo Moncada names a set of barracks in this country that was later attacked at the start of its 1950s revolution.

swap.text: This Paraguayan leader ordered the invasion of Mato Grosso, starting the war. He was later captured and executed at the Battle of Cerro Cora, ending the war.
swap.clue: His demand for his army to have access to Corrientes province led to another conflict, in which his country lost the Humaita fortress and the Battle of Tuyuti.

question.leadin: In 2006 it elected its first female president, Michelle Bachelet.
question.text: Name this country which fought against Bolivia and Peru in the War of the Pacific, and which experienced an earthquake in Concepcion in 1570.
question.clue: After its neighbor imposed a ten cent tax on this country's saltpeter production, this country seized the city of Antofagasta and triggered a war which landlocked that neighbor.

swap.leadin: Activist Joaquim Nabuco led a protest demanding immediate change after this ruler passed the Law of the Free Womb.
swap.text: Name this Brazilian ruler whose daughter Isabel passed the Lei Aurea, or Golden Law, while he was away in Europe.
swap.clue: This man's nation defeated the forces of Juan Manuel de Rosas in the Platine War, during which his army was led by the Duke of Caxias.

question.leadin: Bertha Lutz led a successful push for women's suffrage under this leader.
question.text: Name this Brazilian dictator who stifled the power of "coffee and milk" era oligarchs after establishing the Estado Novo in 1937.
question.clue: This leader first gained office after Washington Luis supported another man from his state as his successor, prompting a coup that ended the politics of coffee with milk.

swap.leadin: A leader with this surname was ordered by a Mendoza judge for testimony and charged with the disappearance of activist Hector Aldo Fagetti Gallego in 1976 during her presidency.
swap.text: Give this surname. Supporters of a general with this surname were killed in the Ezeiza Massacre after he returned to Buenos Aires after an 18-year exile.
swap.clue: Left-wing supporters of a politician with this surname called the Montoneros were attacked by snipers while greeting that politician in the Ezeiza Massacre.

question.text: Os Sertoes, or Revolution in the Backlands, by Brazilian Euclides da Cunha, is the basis for The War of the End of the World, by this Peruvian novelist of Aunt Julia and the Scriptwriter.

swap.leadin: Identify the following about a rebel group.
swap.text: This Sandinista leader, who continues to be active in Nicaraguan politics, was president from 1984 until 1990 when he was defeated by Violeta Barrios de Chamorro.
swap.clue: In 1990, Pedro Chamorro's widow Violetta defeated this Sandanista ruler in the first free presidential elections in over fifty years.

question.text: As part of his surrender conditions, Michimalonco agreed to enroll in this system of Spanish labor. This system essentially let conquistadors enslave the people on the land they conquered.
question.clue: The repartimiento system was intended as a replacement for this policy, which gave owners a number of natives who worked the land in exchange for being converted to Christianity.

swap.text: This leader ordered a failed assassination against Romulo Betancourt ("BET-ahn-coor"), Venezuela's president. This leader ordered the assassination of the Mirabal Sisters.
swap.clue: The novel Feast of the Goat by Mario Vargas Llosa describes the end of this man's reign, as well as his abuse of the wives of his advisors, and after his assassination Joaquin Balaguer was placed in power.

question.text: The Soviets were misled by increased US-UK chatter which was actually due to the diplomatic brouhaha caused by the American attack on this Commonwealth island nation in Operation Urgent Fury.
question.clue: This country's first prime minister was Eric Gairy, whose overthrow led to concerns over the length of Point Salines International Airport and the safety of students at St. George's University.

swap.text: C. L. R. James wrote this book that emphasizes Toussaint L'Ouverture's ("too-sant loo-vair-TOOR's") efforts in leading a successful Haitian Revolution.
swap.answerHtml: The Black Jacobins [or The Black Jacobins: Toussaint l’Ouverture and the San Domingo Revolution]
swap.clue: This history of the Haitian Revolution written by C.L.R. James linked the Haitian struggle with the French Revolution and its ideals.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the dissemination of Rousseau in Spanish America.
question.text: Cecilio Baez's 1910 study of this dictator may have begun the common view that he sought to implement The Social Contract in practice. The doctorate of this first leader of independent Paraguay was actually in theology.
question.answerHtml: Doctor Francia [or José Gaspar Rodríguez de Francia; prompt on El Supremo or Karai Guazu]

swap.leadin: Identify the following about the history of Paraguay FTPE.
swap.text: Alfredo Stroessner was overthrown in 1989 in a coup led by this man, who later succeeded him and began moving Paraguay away from its authoritarian past.

question.text: This man succeeded Mitre as the President of Argentina in 1868, and is best known for policies promoting education. He also wrote Facundo.

swap.leadin: While most famous for being named prima ballerina assoluta of the Royal Ballet, Dame Margot Fonteyn was also arrested in 1959 for smuggling arms by yacht with her husband, a member of this family.
swap.text: Name this Panamanian political family, whose aforementioned member, the paraplegic "Tito,"was the son of Harmodio. This family's most famous member was Arnulfo, a three-time president deposed in three separate coups.
swap.answerHtml: Arias family [or Roberto Emilio Arias, Harmodio Arias Madrid, or Arnulfo Arias Madrid]
